decisions.reason: Although it fits the core cardboard display offer, its appearance only through 2019 suggests it did not become a durable standard and resources are better focused on stronger core solutions.
The pegboard-back variant is close to existing capabilities but was not visibly sustained beyond 2019, indicating insufficient long-term pull to justify keeping another similar format.
This standard quarter-pallet display overlaps heavily with the firm's established range and its short visible market life points to limited differentiation and weak reason to retain it separately.
The eighth-pallet format is a niche extension of the core range and, without evidence of continued market presence after 2019, it is prudent to discontinue it.
The wooden display pallet broadens the offer but is less aligned with the firm's paper-based production focus and its short website presence suggests it was not strong enough to keep.
This media-focused quarter-pallet display is both specialized and no longer visibly marketed after 2019, so dropping it is the sensible choice in a flat industry.
